title: G-ring criterion by formal fibres of the quotients R/q
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Then $R$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] if and only if the following holds for every pair of prime ideals $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $R$: put $B=R/\mathfrak q$ (a domain) and $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q$, let $B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ be the localization of $B$ at $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}/\bar{\mathfrak p}^nB_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ its completion at its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=R_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], which is the fraction field $B_{(0)}$ of $B$; then the $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebra $(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. (The algebra is the formal fibre $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ over $\mathfrak q$.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PN (lemma-check-G-ring-easy, line 12194) and its proof (the identity R_p^ (x)_R kappa(q) = (R/q)_p^ (x)_{R/q} kappa(q)), with the remark after Definition 07GH (line 12160-12191: R_p -> R_p^ is regular iff the formal fibres are geometrically regular)

proof.text: (Notation; Noetherian rings.) Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$; let $\ell_{\mathfrak p}:R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ be the localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $c_{\mathfrak p}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nR_{\mathfrak p}$ the completion map at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}=c_{\mathfrak p}\circ\ell_{\mathfrak p}:R\to(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$ put $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}=(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, the fibre ring of $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$ over $\mathfrak q$, a $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebra. $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. Hence every fibre ring of a ring map into $R_{\mathfrak p}$ or into $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian]; in particular $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $R$.

proof.text: (The completion of the quotient; first part of the identity in the proof of 07PN.) Let $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, $\pi:R\to B=R/\mathfrak q$ the quotient map, $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\pi(\mathfrak p)$, so $\pi^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak p})=\mathfrak p$, and $\ell_B:B\to B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, $c_B:B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\to(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ the localization and the completion at $\bar{\mathfrak p}B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] (with $I=\mathfrak q$) the map $\lambda:R_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, $r/s\mapsto\pi(r)/\pi(s)$, is a surjective ring map with kernel $\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak p}$, and $\lambda\circ\ell_{\mathfrak p}=\ell_B\circ\pi$. Its image of the maximal ideal is $\lambda(\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p})=\bar{\mathfrak p}B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ (both are the sets of sums of elements $\pi(a)/\pi(s)$ with $a\in\mathfrak p$, $s\notin\mathfrak p$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] to the Noetherian local ring $(R_{\mathfrak p},\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p})$ (Step 1) and $\lambda$: the induced map $\theta:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\to(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ satisfies $\theta\circ c_{\mathfrak p}=c_B\circ\lambda$, is surjective, and its kernel is the ideal generated by $c_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak p})$. Since $\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by $\ell_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak q)$, this kernel is the ideal $\mathfrak q(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ generated by $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak q)$. Hence $\theta$ induces a ring isomorphism $\bar\theta:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge/\mathfrak q(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ with $\theta\circ\gamma_{\mathfrak p}=c_B\circ\lambda\circ\ell_{\mathfrak p}=c_B\circ\ell_B\circ\pi$; so $\bar\theta$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras, and, as $\pi$ is surjective, of $B$-algebras (with $B$ acting on the left through $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge/\mathfrak q(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$, on which $\mathfrak q$ acts by $0$, and on the right through $c_B\circ\ell_B$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Section 15.50 (G-rings): Lemma Tag 07PN (lemma-check-G-ring-easy, line 12194) and its proof; the remark before and after Definition Tag 07GH (lines 12160-12191)

proof.text: (The identity $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)=(R/\mathfrak q)^\wedge_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{R/\mathfrak q}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ of the proof of 07PN.) Keep $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and the notation of Step 2. The $R$-algebra map $R\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)=R_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$ kills $\mathfrak q$, so it factors through a ring map $B\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; this is the $B$-algebra structure used in the statement, and it agrees with the inclusion of $B$ into its fraction field $B_{(0)}$ under the isomorphism $R_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}\cong B_{(0)}$, $\overline{r/s}\mapsto\pi(r)/\pi(s)$, of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] (with $I=\mathfrak q$ and the prime $(0)$ of $B$, whose preimage is $\mathfrak q$), which is compatible with the maps from $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (base $R$, the $R$-algebra $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ via $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$, the ideal $\mathfrak q$) $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge/\mathfrak q(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\cong(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RB$, $\bar x\mapsto x\otimes1$; it sends the class of $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}(r)$ to $1\otimes\pi(r)$, so it is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras. With Step 2, $(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge\cong(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RB$ as $B$-algebras. Tensoring with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ over $B$ and applying [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] to $\pi:R\to B$, the $B$-algebra $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and the $R$-algebra $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$, together with the symmetry isomorphisms $X\otimes Y\cong Y\otimes X$, gives isomorphisms of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebras $F_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}:=(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)\otimes_B(B\otimes_R(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)\otimes_R(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\cong E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$.

proof.text: (Fibres away from $\mathfrak p$ vanish.) Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime of $R$ with $\mathfrak q\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and pick $s\in\mathfrak q\setminus\mathfrak p$. Then $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}(s)$ is a unit $u^{-1}$ of $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ (as $\ell_{\mathfrak p}(s)$ is a unit of $R_{\mathfrak p}$) and $s$ maps to $0$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, so in $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$ one has $1\otimes1=u\gamma_{\mathfrak p}(s)\otimes1=u\otimes\bar s=0$: $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$ is the zero ring. The zero ring is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and for every finite purely inseparable extension $k'/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] $k'\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}0=0$ is Noetherian without prime ideals, hence regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] (the condition on localizations is vacuous); so $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, Section 15.50 (G-rings): Lemma Tag 07PN (lemma-check-G-ring-easy, line 12194) and its proof; the remark before and after Definition Tag 07GH (lines 12160-12191)

proof.text: ($c_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular iff $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular.) If $c_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then since $\ell_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular] and every fibre ring $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$ of the composite $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}=c_{\mathfrak p}\circ\ell_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian (Step 1), $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition]. Conversely, if $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}=c_{\mathfrak p}\circ\ell_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular, then $c_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-through-localization] (with $A=R$, $W=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $\psi=c_{\mathfrak p}$). (This is Stacks' remark that the regularity of $R_{\mathfrak p}\to(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ is the geometric regularity of the formal fibres $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, the fibres over the primes $\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak p}$ of $R_{\mathfrak p}$, made precise via the composite with $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$.)

proof.text: ($\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular iff the formal fibres over $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ are geometrically regular.) $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: $\ell_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], $c_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat as $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian (Step 1) [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], and composites of flat maps are flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. So by the definition of a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular iff $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $R$; by Step 4 the primes $\mathfrak q\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$ always satisfy this, so $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular iff $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ for every prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$.

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Being Noetherian and geometrically regular over a field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] is invariant under isomorphisms of $k$-algebras: an isomorphism $\Phi:F\to E$ of $k$-algebras is a ring isomorphism, and $\mathrm{id}_{k'}\otimes\Phi:k'\otimes_kF\to k'\otimes_kE$ is a ring isomorphism for every finite purely inseparable $k'/k$, while being Noetherian and being regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] are invariant under ring isomorphisms. Since $R$ is Noetherian, by the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] $R$ is a G-ring iff $c_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular for every prime $\mathfrak p$, iff (Step 5) $\gamma_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular for every $\mathfrak p$, iff (Step 6) $E_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ for every pair $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, iff (Step 3 and the invariance) $F_{\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p}=(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ for every pair $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, which is the condition of the statement.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 07PN (more-algebra.tex line 12194) and the remark around 07GH (lines 12160-12191); tags 07PN, 07GH, 07BZ, 00MA verified in tags/tags. def-weil-pbc-g-ring requires R_p -> R_p^ regular for every prime p (Stacks 07GH), so no passage between maximal ideals and primes is needed. Proof written in 7 steps: Noetherianity of R_p, R_p^ and of all fibre rings; the identity (R/q)_p^ (x)_{R/q} kappa(q) = R_p^ (x)_R kappa(q) as kappa(q)-algebras (Stacks' proof of 07PN), via R_p -> (R/q)_{p} surjective with kernel qR_p (localization-at-prime-of-quotient), completion of a quotient of a Noetherian local ring (local-completion-quotient), A^/IA^ = A^ (x) A/I (tensor-quotient-base-change) and cancellation of base change; vanishing of the fibres of R -> R_p^ over primes not contained in p; R_p -> R_p^ regular iff R -> R_p^ regular (localization-regular + regular-composition, regular-through-localization), which makes Stacks' 'fibres over the primes qR_p' precise without a separate prime-correspondence node; R -> R_p^ is flat, so it is regular iff the fibres over q in p are Noetherian and geometrically regular. Every step uses existing nodes of unit sk-thm-p1 or definitions; no new node was needed. Statement and stmt_deps kept. The Noetherian clause of the condition is carried through the equivalence (it also holds automatically by Step 1).

reviewed.note: 7 steps: fibres Noetherian; (R/q)_p^ = R_p^/qR_p^ via localization-of-quotient and local-completion-quotient; Stacks' identity via tensor-quotient-base-change and cancel base change; fibres over q not in p vanish; R_p -> R_p^ regular iff R -> R_p^ regular (localization-regular, regular-composition, regular-through-localization); flatness; conclusion. No new nodes. Tags 07PN, 07GH verified. def-weil-pbc-g-ring quantifies over all primes, as Stacks 07GH.

lean.statement: theorem isGRing_iff_pairsOfPrimes (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] : IsGRing R ↔ ∀ (q p : Ideal R) [q.IsPrime] [p.IsPrime] (hqp : q ≤ p), let pbar := p.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk q) letI : pbar.IsPrime := Ideal.isPrime_map_quotientMk_of_isPrime hqp let L := Localization.AtPrime pbar let C := AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal L) L let F := TensorProduct (R ⧸ q) q.ResidueField C IsNoetherianRing F ∧ Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular q.ResidueField F

reviewed_lean.note: R CommRing Noetherian; IsGRing R iff for all primes q<=p: B=R/q, pbar=p.map mk q (prime via isPrime_map_quotientMk_of_isPrime), L=Localization.AtPrime pbar, C=AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal L) L, F=kappa(q) ⊗[B] C (FIBRE RING order, fixed), IsNoetherianRing F ∧ IsGeometricallyRegular kappa(q) F
